thread_analysis.thread_summary: Secom Corporation (contact Hirotaka Kotake, Technology Development Center Safety Products Group) works with Allion (Masaya Iida as primary sales contact, with Itsuo Sakai and Yoshinori Tsuno assisting) on a full Bluetooth SIG certification proxy registration engagement for a security device referencing an EJ2840 Bluetooth module. The thread spans from initial quote request form questions in July 2024 through final registration confirmation in October 2024, covering quote form field guidance, a pricing reclassification due to a SIG site bug, post-order process and documentation questions, future free-registration validity, and proxy registration confirmation form details.
all_questions_found: How should several quote request form fields (Member Class, Model Name, SW/HW Version, Product Description, Product Category, Product Type, wire-transfer checkbox) be filled in?
Why did the proxy registration fee change from ¥150,000 (Single-Design reference) to ¥250,000 (Multi-Design reference)?
What's the timeline from order to registration completion, is a device sample needed, and what additional documents are required?
Is there a time limit on free additional-model registration, or can future similar products always be added?
What does the UserName/Password field on the proxy registration confirmation form refer to, and is it fine to omit future planned devices from the initial registration?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Quote-stage form fields divide into flexible/refinable-later items (description, category, model name format) versus billing-determinative items (Member Class, wire-transfer delegation checkbox). A July 2024 SIG site renewal initially misclassified this registration as Single-Design reference due to a site bug; once fixed, it was correctly reclassified as Multi-Design reference (referencing two existing designs, D044153 and D047621), raising the proxy registration fee from ¥150,000 to ¥250,000. Post-order, the main timeline driver is the ~3-week USD wire transfer lead time; this registration was fully test-exempt (no device sample needed) but still subject to QPRDv3.0 Compliance Folder documentation requirements (manual, block diagram, outline drawing) for the initially-listed representative model. The free additional-model registration benefit is tied to the Bluetooth Core Specification version of the referenced module (EJ2840 = v5.0), valid until v5.0's scheduled retirement date of February 1, 2032; already-listed models remain sellable indefinitely afterward absent new SIG rules. The proxy registration confirmation form's credential field requires the customer's own SIG account (with a recommended post-registration password change), and future devices don't need to be pre-listed since free derivative-model registration is available anytime via self-service web operations.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: Registration fee tiers and free-addition validity windows are governed by objective technical factors (number of referenced designs, Bluetooth Core Spec version retirement schedule) rather than arbitrary pricing or fixed multi-year limits; proxy registration mechanically requires use of the customer's own account credentials since the registering party acts as the customer during the process.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Misexplaining a fee reclassification as an arbitrary increase could damage customer trust; failing to flag the QPRDv3.0 Compliance Folder requirement despite test exemption could leave the customer non-compliant if audited; giving a vague answer about free-registration validity could lead to mistaken assumptions about a fixed expiration or no expiration at all.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: None identified — Allion (primarily via Sakai's drafted responses sent under Iida's name) consistently provided clear, technically grounded explanations for each pricing and process question raised.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When fee classifications or process requirements change due to underlying technical factors (site bugs, spec version retirement schedules, post-rule-change documentation requirements), proactively explain the specific technical driver behind the change rather than leaving the customer to assume an arbitrary increase or omission.
